webTreeSitter.note: MEASURED 2026-09-27 by script/m60/measure-runtime-stragglers.ts (evidence: validation/m60/results/M60.0.runtime-stragglers.json): moving this pin to 0.27.0 breaks 19 of 61 shipped grammar wasms — every core web language among them (javascript, typescript, tsx, java, go, html, json, ruby, swift, zig, vue). The cause is NOT an API break: 0.27.0 calls getDylinkMetadata() and refuses a grammar wasm without the newer emscripten dylink.0 section. That correspondence is now MEASURED rather than asserted: {0.27.0 load failures} == {shipped wasms lacking dylink.0}, exactly, confirmed. A wasm built by tree-sitter CLI 0.26.9 carries that section and loads on BOTH runtimes, so the migration is a REBUILD of the stragglers, not a version bump. Until that rebuild is done and measured, 0.25.9 is the correct pin.

harnessControl.why: three deliberate corruptions of a working grammar must fail to load on every runtime, checked BEFORE any result is read. The first version of this harness stopped at the lazy Language.load() and reported 61/61 for a tree containing a truncated wasm, a clobbered magic number and a scrambled payload. A harness that cannot detect failure cannot certify success.

sources.raw: - Parser: `tree-sitter-cpp`, **a LOCAL FORK of upstream 0.23.4** — not the npm package. (This section previously said "0.23.4 (npm, latest)", which was false: the wired wasm was never the npm bytes, and the byte lengths of the two differ by ~118 KB.)

candidates.knownLimit: --sample 400 does not complete: the G2 s-expression comparison dies with `call_indirect to a signature that does not match` at C._ts_node_to_string_wasm. NOT an ABI mismatch — all three wasms report language.version 15 and toString() succeeds on all three for a trivial parse. It is input-dependent: the fsharp grammar exhausts the fixed web-tree-sitter heap on the compiler's largest files, the same fragility that appears as a ts_malloc_default abort when walking the 6,627-file corpus. Future fsharp grammar decisions are gated at --sample 250 or below, with the sample stated so two runs are comparable.

limitations: This registry records IDENTITY, PROVENANCE and UPSTREAM STATE. It does not measure parse quality; that is validation/m12/results/*-corpus-errors.json and validation/m14/results/M14.0.F10.json, and the `evidence` block here is DERIVED from those files rather than authored beside them.
A declared version is a PROSE CLAIM. Where no version is declared the lane is recorded as `versionKnown: false` and its staleness as `unknown` — never defaulted to `current`.
`staleness.behind` is a semver comparison against upstream's latest tag, not a capability judgement. A grammar can be the newest release and still be the weakest parser for a language.

Candidate discovery searches the npm registry and resolves identity by REPOSITORY, not by package name: `tree-sitter-sql` on npm is a 2021 stub at 0.1.0 with no repository, and a name-keyed upgrade would silently install it.
A candidate listed here is not endorsed. `verdict` is `unmeasured` for every candidate in this file by construction.
The lane->grammar map is parsed out of src/ast/engine.ts, so it cannot drift from the loader. The npm/repo identity is still prose-derived and is the weakest field in the row.
